answer: No identity can exist without a unique graph position and bonded backing. Each agent must register at one unoccupied vertex on a shared trust graph; consensus rejects collisions, so duplicate claims fail. Registration burns a jade bond tied to that vertex, and two existing neighbors must co-sign, with both stakes slashed if they vouch for a sybil. Agents also publish a signed sonnet as a public commitment. Names multiply, but graph rent and guarantors do not.
